# Adjudication Task — Chapter 330

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃330화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|자정 무렵.
  6|
  7|용봉표국을 나선 네 사람의 신형이 사라지는 것은 그야말로 순식간이었다.
  8|
  9|불어오는 찬 바람에 함께 마중 나온 용봉표국의 식솔들은 몸을 떨었지만, 주화란은 미동도 없이 그 자리에 서 있었다.
 10|
 11|마치 조금만 더 기다리면 누군가 다시 돌아오기라도 할 것처럼.
 12|
 13|그렇게 짙은 어둠을 바라보던 그때였다.
 14|
 15|“떠났군.”
 16|
 17|기척도 없이 불쑥 들려온 목소리에 화들짝 놀란 표사들이 양옆으로 갈라졌다. 그러나 주화란은 동요하지 않았다.
 18|
 19|“네, 떠났네요.”
 20|
 21|“아쉬운가?”
 22|
 23|“아쉽지 않다면 거짓말이겠죠.”
 24|
 25|“별수 없어. 떠날 사람은 떠나고, 남을 사람은 남고. 그게 순리인 거지.”
 26|
 27|“순리…….”
 28|
 29|작게 중얼거린 주화란이 천천히 돌아섰다.
 30|
 31|“송 표두는 어느 쪽인가요?”
 32|
 33|“나?”
 34|
 35|피식 웃은 송일섬이 어깨에 짊어진 행낭(行囊)을 보란 듯이 흔들었다.
 36|
 37|“어느 쪽일 것 같나?”
 38|
 39|“그게 술에 취해 잠든 척했던 이유인가요?”
 40|
 41|“자그마치 십 년이야. 이 정도면 도리는 다했다고 보는데…… 아직 부족한가?”
 42|
 43|“네.”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|“부족합니다. 아직 도리를 다하지 않으셨어요.”
 48|
 49|망설임 없는 주화란의 대답에 송일섬이 미간을 찌푸렸다.
 50|
 51|“아직 부족하다고? 십 년 동안 용봉표국을, 널 지켰는데도 말이냐?”
 52|
 53|“제 조부께서 베푸신 구명지은(救命知恩)에 비할까요?”
 54|
 55|“너……!”
 56|
 57|송일섬의 목소리를 키우며 걸음을 내딛자, 주위에 있던 표사들이 흠칫 놀라며 검자루를 움켜잡았다.
 58|
 59|그의 출신 성분에 숨겨진 내막을 듣지 못한 그들에게 있어 송일섬은 아직까지 경계해야 할 대상이었다. 특히 그와 함께 용봉삼표에 속한 또 다른 두 명의 표두는 적의마저 드러냈다.
 60|
 61|“목소리 낮추게. 그게 신상에 이로울 게야.”
 62|
 63|“소국주께서는 어찌 생각하실지 모르나, 우리는 아닐세. 아무리 생각해도 자네가 영 수상쩍단 말이지.”
 64|
 65|두 표두가 굳은 얼굴로 송일섬을 가로막은 그때였다.
 66|
 67|“그만. 물러가세요.”
 68|
 69|주화란의 덤덤한 목소리에 두 표두가 말을 더듬었다.
 70|
 71|“소, 소국주.”
 72|
 73|“하지만 이자는 아직 혐의를 완전히 벗지 않았……!”
 74|
 75|“물러나라 했습니다. 긴히 나눌 이야기가 있으니 모두 자리로 돌아가 남은 일들을 처리하세요.”
 76|
 77|“으음…….”
 78|
 79|“아, 알겠습니다.”
 80|
 81|할 말이 있는 것처럼 입술을 달싹이던 두 표두가 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 82|
 83|이내 다른 표사들을 데리고 천천히 멀어지는 그들의 뒷모습을 바라보던 송일섬이 주화란을 향해 혀를 찼다.
 84|
 85|“충성스러운 건지, 멍청한 건지 도무지 분간이 안 되는군. 이 지경까지 왔는데도 적아(敵我)를 구분 못 하다니.”
 86|
 87|“전제가 틀렸어요.”
 88|
 89|“뭐?”
 90|
 91|“저들은 송 표두의 생각처럼 충성스럽지도 않고, 멍청하지도 않으니까요.”
 92|
 93|순간 송일섬의 뇌리에 한 가지 의문이 스쳤다.
 94|
 95|‘혹시?’
 96|
 97|깨달음은 찰나였다.
 98|
 99|타고난 싸움꾼이자 천생 무인인 그였지만, 그렇다고 해서 머리까지 나쁜 것은 아니었다.
100|
101|사태를 파악한 송일섬이 작게 중얼거렸다.
102|
103|“이거 원, 요지경이 따로 없군.”
104|
105|주화란이 고개를 끄덕였다.
106|
107|“의도적으로 표행과 계약을 망치고, 혼란한 틈을 타 자금을 빼돌렸으며 교묘하게 장부를 조작했습니다. 허 숙부가 이 모든 것을 홀로 했을 리 없죠.”
108|
109|“도대체 어디서부터 어디까지 연관된 거지?”
110|
111|“정확한 숫자와 신상은 지금부터 파악해야겠지만…… 최소한 두 사람은 포함시켜야겠죠.”
112|
113|주화란의 시선이 서서히 멀어지는 두 표두의 뒷모습을 훑고 송일섬에게 닿았다.
114|
115|“이참에 뿌리 뽑을 겁니다.”
116|
117|“차라리 총표두를 죽인 자리에서 밝히지 그랬나?”
118|
119|“혼란이 가중되었을 거예요. 그리고 이것조차 제힘으로 해내지 못하면, 용봉표국의 소국주가 될 자격이 없겠죠.”
120|
121|“자신은 있고?”
122|
123|주화란이 물끄러미 송일섬을 응시했다.
124|
125|“지금 들고 계신 행낭, 일 년 후에 다시 꺼내시는 건 어떨까요?”
126|
127|“나를 이용해 발본색원(拔本塞源)하겠다?”
128|
129|“송 표두. 지금 전 누구든 벨 수 있을 만큼 날카로운 검이 필요합니다. 마침 적임자가 제 눈앞에 있고요.”
130|
131|“거절한다. 그리고 이제 표두라고 부르는 것 따윈 집어치워.”
132|
133|“그럼 추혼객(追魂客)을 고용하는 건 어떤가요?”
134|
135|“뭐?”
136|
137|주화란이 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
138|
139|“천하의 추혼객이니 비용이 제법 나가겠지만…… 과거의 인연이 있으니 어느 정도는 감안해 주시겠죠?”
140|
141|“그것으로 구명지은을 갚아라?”
142|
143|“그랬다면 더 큰 걸 요구했겠죠.”
144|
145|“아까는 표왕께서 베푼 구명지은에 도리를 다하지 않았다더니?”
146|
147|“그거야 보는 눈이 많았으니까. 제 조부께서도 말씀하셨어요. 사람이 사람을 구한 것뿐이라고.”
148|
149|“하!”
150|
151|송일섬은 참지 못하고 웃음을 터트렸다.
152|
153|십 년 전, 빛바랜 옥비녀를 들고 찾아온 앳된 청년에게 군자검 주호군이 건넨 말이 떠올라서다.
154|
155|
156|
157|‘비록 한 대(代)를 건너 만났으나, 이제라도 찾아와 주었으니 그것으로 되었네. 전 대의 인연에 얽매이지 말고 자네의 삶을 살게.’
158|
159|‘예?’
160|
161|‘선친께서 말씀하셨지. 당신께서 한 일은 사람이 사람을 구한 것뿐이라고. 내 생각도 그와 같다네. 그리고…… 이리 훌륭히 장성해 주어 고맙네.’
162|
163|
164|
165|충격이었다.
166|
167|어린 시절부터 송일섬의 삶은 투쟁의 연속이었다. 부모는 요절했고 하나뿐인 유일한 버팀 막이던 조모마저 운명했을 때, 그는 누구 하나 도와주는 이 없이 혼자서 헤쳐나와야 했다.
168|
169|시체 더미에서 병장기를 찾아 훔쳤고, 정당한 대가를 빼앗으려는 낭인의 목을 베었으며 숱한 생사결을 통해 자신을 입증해 왔다.
170|
171|‘뭔가를 요구할 줄 알았는데.’
172|
173|낭인으로 살아온 송일섬에게는 그것이 당연했다.
174|
175|설령 주호군이 누군가를 없애고 싶어 한다면, 그는 기꺼이 그랬을 것이다. 기분은 더럽겠지만 항상 해 왔던 일이니까.
176|
177|지금까지 해결한 수많은 의뢰, 그중 하나에 불과했다.
178|
179|하지만…… 주호군은 달랐다.
180|
181|그는 송일섬이 천애 고아가 된 이후 처음으로 만난 ‘어른’이었다.
182|
183|그래서였을지도 모른다, 엉겁결에 한마디가 튀어나온 것은.
184|
185|
186|
187|‘십 년.’
188|
189|‘응?’
190|
191|‘십 년 후 떠나겠습니다. 비록 배운 것이라고는 사람 죽이는 것밖에 없는 몸이지만, 행여 무슨 일이 생기더라도 국주님과 아이만큼은 지키겠습니다. 수십 년 전 표왕께서 그러셨던 것처럼.’
192|
193|
194|
195|송일섬은 맹세를 지켰다.
196|
197|용봉표국의 표사가 되어 명령에 충실히 따랐고, 표국에 머무르는 동안은 국주의 부탁에 따라 그의 여식을 그림자처럼 따라다니며 지켰다.
198|
199|세월이 흘러 아이가 아름다운 규수로 장성하자 그와 관련하여 이상한 소문이 돌았으나 개의치 않았다.
200|
201|국주가 쓰러져도, 표국이 무너져도 송일섬은 묵묵히 그 자리를 지켰다.
202|
203|‘그저 도리를 다할 뿐.’
204|
205|송일섬은 굳게 감고 있던 눈을 떴다. 그리고 자신을 바라보고 있는 주화란을 향해 불쑥 입을 열었다.
206|
207|“나는 달포 후 떠난다.”
208|
209|“……!”
210|
211|“네가 배반자들의 정체를 알아내면, 내가 앞장서서 솎아내 주마. 달포면 충분할 것이다.”
212|
213|주화란의 표정을 본 송일섬이 무뚝뚝하게 말했다.
214|
215|“그런 얼굴 할 것 없다. 함양(咸陽)에 들러 영약을 구해 오는 것뿐이니.”
216|
217|“영약……이요?”
218|
219|“그래. 그것이라면 국주님의 병세를 치료할 수 있을 것이다. 애초에 천년설삼은 힘이 너무 과하여 역효과가 날 수 있지만, 이번에 구한 영약은 확실히 효력을 볼 수 있을 거야.”
220|
221|“어, 어떻게 그만한 영약을…….”
222|
223|“됐어. 입 아프니 더는 묻지 마라.”
224|
225|송일섬이 손을 내저었다.
226|
227|이 년이 넘도록 수소문한 끝에 어렵게 구한 영약이다. 천년설삼 같은 희대의 영약은 아니었지만 주화입마에 빠진 국주를 회복시키는 데에는 다른 무엇보다 적격이었다.
228|
229|덕분에 추혼객으로 벌었던 막대한 재산을 모조리 털어 넣어야 했지만, 재물이야 모으면 그만이다.
230|
231|“그거 알아?”
232|
233|송일섬의 덤덤한 목소리가 이어졌다.
234|
235|“사람이 사람을 살리는 것만큼 어려운 일도 없어. 네게는 당연하게 생각했던 일이…… 내게는 가장 어려운 일이었다.”
236|
237|송일섬은 지금까지 사람을 죽이는 것을 업으로 삼았다.
238|
239|그랬던 그가 누군가를 지키게 된 것은, 용봉표국에 들어온 이후였다.
240|
241|“송 표두…….”
242|
243|젖은 눈동자로 그를 바라보던 주화란이 송일섬의 좁혀진 미간을 보고 황급히 말을 고쳤다.
244|
245|“아, 송 대협.”
246|
247|“언제까지 헷갈릴 셈이냐.”
248|
249|“죄송해요. 너무 놀라서 순간적으로…….”
250|
251|“그럼 이참에 직책 하나 만들지 그래.”
252|
253|“네?”
254|
255|“총표두는 싫다. 표행도 젬병이고, 사람도 다뤄야 하니까.”
256|
257|“네, 네?”
258|
259|“호위당주. 그래, 그걸로 하면 좋겠군.”
260|
261|주화란이 어어, 하는 사이 송일섬은 등을 돌려 걸음을 옮겼다.
262|
263|어둠이 내려앉은 문밖이 아닌, 자신의 거처를 향해서.
264|
265|“행낭은 싸지 말걸.”
266|
267|나지막한 중얼거림을 흘리며 멀어지는 송일섬의 뒷모습을 바라보던 주화란의 입가에 보조개가 패었다.
268|
269|
270|
271|* * *
272|
273|
274|
275|쏴아아아.
276|
277|팽팽한 돛대와 물살을 가르는 선미.
278|
279|그렇게 바람처럼 나아가는 쾌조선(快調船)에는 구릿빛 상체를 드러낸 사내들이 밧줄을 당기고, 노를 저었다. 갑판에 모습을 드러낸 이들의 머릿수만 족히 오십에 달했다.
280|
281|그런 쾌조선이 다섯 척이니, 족히 삼백에 달하는 병력인 셈이었다.
282|
283|“더, 더 빨리!”
284|
285|“이놈들아. 그리 굼떠서 어찌 수룡채(水龍砦)의 일원이라 할 수 있겠느냐!”
286|
287|수룡채는 장강수로맹(長江水路盟)에 속한 대형 수채였다.
288|
289|그들은 자신들을 장강의 영웅들이라 부르며 자랑스러워했지만, 양민들이 부르는 이름은 영웅과는 썩 거리가 멀었다.
290|
291|“수적! 수적이다!”
292|
293|“아니, 저 썅노무 새끼들이 왜 여길!”
294|
295|다섯 척의 쾌조선을 발견한 선주(船主)는 자리에 털썩 주저앉았다.
296|
297|상대는 어중이떠중이가 아닌 장강수로맹의 수룡채다. 저들의 쾌조선은 따라잡을 수도 없고, 전투는 감히 생각조차 할 수 없다.
298|
299|‘일진 제대로 꼬였군.’
300|

“My father said that all he had done was one person saving another. I feel the same way. And…thank you for growing into such a fine young man.”

[P79]
It had been a shock.

[P80]
From childhood onward, Song Ilseom’s life had been one continuous struggle. His parents had died young, and when his only source of support—his grandmother—passed away as well, he had been forced to make his way alone, without anyone’s help.

[P81]
He had stolen weapons from piles of corpses, cut down wandering martial artists who tried to rob him of his rightful pay, and proven himself through countless life-and-death duels.

[P82]
*I thought he would ask me for something.*

[P83]
To Song Ilseom, who had lived as a wandering martial artist, that was only natural.

[P84]
If Ju Hogun had wanted someone eliminated, Song Ilseom would have willingly done it. It would have left a bad taste in his mouth, but killing was what he had always done.

[P85]
It would have been just one more among the countless requests he had completed.

[P86]
But Ju Hogun had been different.

[P87]
He was the first “adult” Song Ilseom had met since becoming an orphan with no one in the world.

[P88]
Perhaps that was why the words had slipped out before he could think.

[P89]
“Ten years.”

[P90]
“Hmm?”

[P91]
“I’ll leave after ten years. Though all I know is how to kill, I’ll protect you and your child no matter what happens. Just as the Escort King did several decades ago.”

[P92]
Song Ilseom had kept his oath.

[P93]
He became an escort of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and faithfully followed orders. While he remained at the bureau, he followed the Chief’s daughter like a shadow and protected her at her father’s request.

[P94]
As the years passed and the child grew into a beautiful young woman, strange rumors began circulating about the two of them, but he paid them no mind.

[P95]
Even when the Chief collapsed and the Escort Bureau began to crumble, Song Ilseom silently remained at his post.

[P96]
*I’m only doing my duty.*

[P97]
Song Ilseom opened his tightly shut eyes and abruptly spoke to Ju Hwaran, who had been watching him.

[P98]
“I’m leaving in a fortnight.”

[P99]
“…!”

[P100]
“If you discover the traitors’ identities, I’ll take the lead in weeding them out. A fortnight should be enough.”

[P101]
Seeing Ju Hwaran’s expression, Song Ilseom added bluntly, “Don’t make that face. I’m only going to Xianyang to pick up an elixir.”

[P102]
“An elixir?”

[P103]
“That’s right. It should be able to cure the Chief’s illness. The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was too potent and might have done more harm than good, but this elixir should definitely work.”

[P104]
“H-how did you obtain an elixir like that…?”

[P105]
“Enough. I’m tired of talking, so don’t ask any more questions.”

[P106]
Song Ilseom waved a hand.

[P107]
He had managed to secure the elixir after more than two years of searching. It was not a legendary treasure like the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, but nothing else was better suited to restoring the Chief after his qi deviation.

[P108]
It had cost him every last coin of the enormous fortune he had earned as the Soul-Chasing Guest, but money could always be earned again.

[P109]
“Do you know something?”

[P110]
Song Ilseom continued in a quiet voice.

[P111]
“There’s nothing harder than saving a person’s life. What you took for granted…was the hardest thing in the world for me.”

[P112]
Song Ilseom had made his living by killing people.

[P113]
It was only after joining the Yongbong Escort Bureau that he began protecting someone instead.

[P114]
“Captain Song…”

[P115]
Ju Hwaran stared at him with glistening eyes, but when she saw his furrowed brow, she hastily corrected herself.

[P116]
“Ah, Great Hero Song.”

[P117]
“How long are you going to keep getting that wrong?”

[P118]
“I’m sorry. I was so surprised that it slipped out…”

[P119]
“Then why don’t you create a position while you’re at it?”

[P120]
“Pardon?”

[P121]
“I don’t want to be Chief Escort. I’m terrible at escort missions, and I’d have to manage people.”

[P122]
“P-pardon?”

[P123]
“Guard Hall Master. Yes, that will do.”

[P124]
While Ju Hwaran was still stammering, Song Ilseom turned and walked away.

[P125]
Not toward the gate and the darkness beyond it, but toward his own quarters.

[P126]
“I shouldn’t have packed my bag.”

[P127]
Dimples appeared in Ju Hwaran’s cheeks as she watched Song Ilseom recede into the distance, his quiet mutter trailing behind him.

[P128]
* * *

[P129]
*Whoosh!*

[P130]
Sails stretched taut and sterns sliced through the current as the swift ships raced forward like the wind. Bare-chested, bronze-skinned men hauled on ropes and pulled at the oars. At least fifty men could be seen on the deck of each ship.

[P131]
With five swift ships in all, their force numbered nearly three hundred.

[P132]
“Faster! Faster!”

[P133]
“You louts! How can you call yourselves members of the Water Dragon Stronghold when you’re that slow?”

[P134]
The Water Dragon Stronghold was a major river stronghold belonging to the Yangtze River Channel League.

[P135]
Its members proudly called themselves the heroes of the Yangtze, but ordinary people had a rather less flattering name for them.

[P136]
“River bandits! They’re river bandits!”

[P137]
“Why the hell are those bastards here?”

[P138]
The shipmaster who spotted the five swift ships dropped where he stood.

[P139]
These were no ragtag thugs. They were the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There was no outrunning their swift ships, and fighting them was out of the question.

[P140]
*This day has gone completely to hell.*

[P141]
There was only one way to get through this quietly.

[P142]
Looking utterly dejected, the shipmaster called over the youngest sailor passing by.

[P143]
“Hey!”

[P144]
“Yes, shipmaster.”

[P145]
“Tell the passengers to pay up.”

[P146]
“Pardon?”

[P147]
“Collect their money! We have a toll to pay!”

[P148]
The fact that the bandits belonged to the Yangtze River Channel League was both a curse and a blessing. Once they caught you, there was no escaping, but at least they did not start swinging their swords without warning.

[P149]
The Yangtze River Channel League claimed this set them apart from the common river-bandit rabble found everywhere under heaven, but one pack of bastards was much the same as another.

[P150]
“Damn it… There goes today’s profit.”

[P151]
The shipmaster was heaving sigh after sigh when someone tapped him on the shoulder.

[P152]
“Excuse me.”

[P153]
“Gah! You startled me! Who are you?”

[P154]
“I’m a passenger.”

[P155]
“I know that.”

[P156]
The shipmaster studied the young man who had appeared out of nowhere. Judging by the sword at his waist, he seemed to be a martial artist, but…

[P157]
*He looks kind of dopey. That mouth of his sticks out, too. Bet he never shuts up.*

[P158]
Third-rate martial artists were a dime a dozen.

[P159]
It was hardly his first time dealing with one. The shipmaster sighed.

[P160]
“What do you want? If this is about the money, I’ve got nothing to say. Go back to your seat. Don’t try anything stupid and end up crossing the Sanzu River.”[^1]

[P161]
The young man watched the swift ships drawing rapidly closer.

[P162]
“Are they river bandits?”

[P163]
“Can’t you tell by looking? They’re from the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There isn’t a soul in Sichuan who doesn’t know them.”

[P164]
“The Yangtze River Channel League…”

[P165]
“Running won’t help. You’ll never escape those swift ships. Once they spot you, it’s over. Completely over!”

[P166]
“Those ships must be pretty fast.”

[P167]
“What kind of question is—”

[P168]
The shipmaster was about to snap at him when he sucked in a breath and clamped his mouth shut.

[P169]
A shadow had risen behind the young man, a full head taller than him.

[P170]
The giant had shaggy hair, and a great mound of hides rose high atop the pack frame on his back.

[P171]
He stared blankly at the shipmaster, then spoke to the young man.

[P172]
“Mujin.”

[P173]
“Yes?”

[P174]
“Let’s take that ship.”

[P175]
The shipmaster wondered if he had heard correctly.

[P176]
[^1]: The Sanzu River is a Buddhist river believed to mark the boundary between life and death.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P82]
*I thought he would ask me for something.*

[P83]
To Song Ilseom, who had lived as a wandering martial artist, that was only natural.

[P84]
If Ju Hogun had wanted someone eliminated, Song Ilseom would have willingly done it. It would have left a bad taste in his mouth, but killing was what he had always done.

[P85]
It would have been just one more among the countless requests he had completed.

[P86]
But Ju Hogun had been different.

[P87]
He was the first “adult” Song Ilseom had met since becoming an orphan with no one in the world.

[P88]
Perhaps that was why the words had slipped out before he could think.

[P89]
“Ten years.”

[P90]
“Hmm?”

[P91]
“I’ll leave after ten years. Though all I know is how to kill, I’ll protect you and your child no matter what happens. Just as the Escort King did several decades ago.”

[P92]
Song Ilseom had kept his oath.

[P93]
He became an escort of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and faithfully followed orders. While he remained at the bureau, he followed the Chief’s daughter like a shadow and protected her at her father’s request.

[P94]
As the years passed and the child grew into a beautiful young woman, strange rumors began circulating about the two of them, but he paid them no mind.

[P95]
Even when the Chief collapsed and the Escort Bureau began to crumble, Song Ilseom silently remained at his post.

[P96]
*I’m only doing my duty.*

[P97]
Song Ilseom opened his tightly shut eyes and abruptly spoke to Ju Hwaran, who had been watching him.

[P98]
“I’m leaving in a fortnight.”

[P99]
“…!”

[P100]
“If you discover the traitors’ identities, I’ll take the lead in weeding them out. A fortnight should be enough.”

[P101]
Seeing Ju Hwaran’s expression, Song Ilseom added bluntly, “Don’t make that face. I’m only going to Xianyang to pick up an elixir.”

[P102]
“An elixir?”

[P103]
“That’s right. It should be able to cure the Chief’s illness. The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was too potent and might have done more harm than good, but this elixir should definitely work.”

[P104]
“H-how did you obtain an elixir like that…?”

[P105]
“Enough. I’m tired of talking, so don’t ask any more questions.”

[P106]
Song Ilseom waved a hand.

[P107]
He had managed to secure the elixir after more than two years of searching. It was not a legendary treasure like the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, but nothing else was better suited to restoring the Chief after his qi deviation.

[P108]
It had cost him every last coin of the enormous fortune he had earned as the Soul-Chasing Guest, but money could always be earned again.

[P109]
“Do you know something?”

[P110]
Song Ilseom continued in a quiet voice.

[P111]
“There’s nothing harder than saving a person’s life. What you took for granted…was the hardest thing in the world for me.”

[P112]
Song Ilseom had made his living by killing people.

[P113]
It was only after joining the Yongbong Escort Bureau that he began protecting someone instead.

[P114]
“Captain Song…”

[P115]
Ju Hwaran stared at him with glistening eyes, but when she saw his furrowed brow, she hastily corrected herself.

[P116]
“Ah, Great Hero Song.”

[P117]
“How long are you going to keep getting that wrong?”

[P118]
“I’m sorry. I was so surprised that it slipped out…”

[P119]
“Then why don’t you create a position while you’re at it?”

[P120]
“Pardon?”

[P121]
“I don’t want to be Chief Escort. I’m terrible at escort missions, and I’d have to manage people.”

[P122]
“P-pardon?”

[P123]
“Guard Hall Master. Yes, that will do.”

[P124]
While Ju Hwaran was still stammering, Song Ilseom turned and walked away.

[P125]
Not toward the gate and the darkness beyond it, but toward his own quarters.

[P126]
“I shouldn’t have packed my bag.”

[P127]
Dimples appeared in Ju Hwaran’s cheeks as she watched Song Ilseom recede into the distance, his quiet mutter trailing behind him.

[P128]
* * *

[P129]
*Whoosh!*

[P130]
Sails stretched taut and sterns sliced through the current as the swift ships raced forward like the wind. Bare-chested, bronze-skinned men hauled on ropes and pulled at the oars. At least fifty men could be seen on the deck of each ship.

[P131]
With five swift ships in all, their force numbered nearly three hundred.

[P132]
“Faster! Faster!”

[P133]
“You louts! How can you call yourselves members of the Water Dragon Stronghold when you’re that slow?”

[P134]
The Water Dragon Stronghold was a major river stronghold belonging to the Yangtze River Channel League.

[P135]
Its members proudly called themselves the heroes of the Yangtze, but ordinary people had a rather less flattering name for them.

[P136]
“River bandits! They’re river bandits!”

[P137]
“Why the hell are those bastards here?”

[P138]
The shipmaster who spotted the five swift ships dropped where he stood.

[P139]
These were no ragtag thugs. They were the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There was no outrunning their swift ships, and fighting them was out of the question.

[P140]
*This day has gone completely to hell.*

[P141]
There was only one way to get through this quietly.

[P142]
Looking utterly dejected, the shipmaster called over the youngest sailor passing by.

[P143]
“Hey!”

[P144]
“Yes, shipmaster.”

[P145]
“Tell the passengers to pay up.”

[P146]
“Pardon?”

[P147]
“Collect their money! We have a toll to pay!”

[P148]
The fact that the bandits belonged to the Yangtze River Channel League was both a curse and a blessing. Once they caught you, there was no escaping, but at least they did not start swinging their swords without warning.

[P149]
The Yangtze River Channel League claimed this set them apart from the common river-bandit rabble found everywhere under heaven, but one pack of bastards was much the same as another.

[P150]
“Damn it… There goes today’s profit.”

[P151]
The shipmaster was heaving sigh after sigh when someone tapped him on the shoulder.

[P152]
“Excuse me.”

[P153]
“Gah! You startled me! Who are you?”

[P154]
“I’m a passenger.”

[P155]
“I know that.”

[P156]
The shipmaster studied the young man who had appeared out of nowhere. Judging by the sword at his waist, he seemed to be a martial artist, but…

[P157]
*He looks kind of dopey. That mouth of his sticks out, too. Bet he never shuts up.*

[P158]
Third-rate martial artists were a dime a dozen.

[P159]
It was hardly his first time dealing with one. The shipmaster sighed.

[P160]
“What do you want? If this is about the money, I’ve got nothing to say. Go back to your seat. Don’t try anything stupid and end up crossing the Sanzu River.”[^1]

[P161]
The young man watched the swift ships drawing rapidly closer.

[P162]
“Are they river bandits?”

[P163]
“Can’t you tell by looking? They’re from the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There isn’t a soul in Sichuan who doesn’t know them.”

[P164]
“The Yangtze River Channel League…”

[P165]
“Running won’t help. You’ll never escape those swift ships. Once they spot you, it’s over. Completely over!”

[P166]
“Those ships must be pretty fast.”

[P167]
“What kind of question is—”

[P168]
The shipmaster was about to snap at him when he sucked in a breath and clamped his mouth shut.

[P169]
A shadow had risen behind the young man, a full head taller than him.

[P170]
The giant had shaggy hair, and a great mound of hides rose high atop the pack frame on his back.

[P171]
He stared blankly at the shipmaster, then spoke to the young man.

[P172]
“Mujin.”

[P173]
“Yes?”

[P174]
“Let’s take that ship.”

[P175]
The shipmaster wondered if he had heard correctly.

[P176]
[^1]: The Sanzu River is a Buddhist river believed to mark the boundary between life and death.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 330

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃330화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|자정 무렵.
  6|
  7|용봉표국을 나선 네 사람의 신형이 사라지는 것은 그야말로 순식간이었다.
  8|
  9|불어오는 찬 바람에 함께 마중 나온 용봉표국의 식솔들은 몸을 떨었지만, 주화란은 미동도 없이 그 자리에 서 있었다.
 10|
 11|마치 조금만 더 기다리면 누군가 다시 돌아오기라도 할 것처럼.
 12|
 13|그렇게 짙은 어둠을 바라보던 그때였다.
 14|
 15|“떠났군.”
 16|
 17|기척도 없이 불쑥 들려온 목소리에 화들짝 놀란 표사들이 양옆으로 갈라졌다. 그러나 주화란은 동요하지 않았다.
 18|
 19|“네, 떠났네요.”
 20|
 21|“아쉬운가?”
 22|
 23|“아쉽지 않다면 거짓말이겠죠.”
 24|
 25|“별수 없어. 떠날 사람은 떠나고, 남을 사람은 남고. 그게 순리인 거지.”
 26|
 27|“순리…….”
 28|
 29|작게 중얼거린 주화란이 천천히 돌아섰다.
 30|
 31|“송 표두는 어느 쪽인가요?”
 32|
 33|“나?”
 34|
 35|피식 웃은 송일섬이 어깨에 짊어진 행낭(行囊)을 보란 듯이 흔들었다.
 36|
 37|“어느 쪽일 것 같나?”
 38|
 39|“그게 술에 취해 잠든 척했던 이유인가요?”
 40|
 41|“자그마치 십 년이야. 이 정도면 도리는 다했다고 보는데…… 아직 부족한가?”
 42|
 43|“네.”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|“부족합니다. 아직 도리를 다하지 않으셨어요.”
 48|
 49|망설임 없는 주화란의 대답에 송일섬이 미간을 찌푸렸다.
 50|
 51|“아직 부족하다고? 십 년 동안 용봉표국을, 널 지켰는데도 말이냐?”
 52|
 53|“제 조부께서 베푸신 구명지은(救命知恩)에 비할까요?”
 54|
 55|“너……!”
 56|
 57|송일섬의 목소리를 키우며 걸음을 내딛자, 주위에 있던 표사들이 흠칫 놀라며 검자루를 움켜잡았다.
 58|
 59|그의 출신 성분에 숨겨진 내막을 듣지 못한 그들에게 있어 송일섬은 아직까지 경계해야 할 대상이었다. 특히 그와 함께 용봉삼표에 속한 또 다른 두 명의 표두는 적의마저 드러냈다.
 60|
 61|“목소리 낮추게. 그게 신상에 이로울 게야.”
 62|
 63|“소국주께서는 어찌 생각하실지 모르나, 우리는 아닐세. 아무리 생각해도 자네가 영 수상쩍단 말이지.”
 64|

# Chapter 330

[P2]
Around midnight.

[P3]
The four figures who had left the Yongbong Escort Bureau disappeared in the blink of an eye.

[P4]
The members of the bureau who had come out to see them off shivered in the cold wind, but Ju Hwaran stood there without moving.

[P5]
As if someone might come back if she waited just a little longer.

[P6]
It was then that she heard a voice from the darkness.

[P7]
“They’re gone.”

[P8]
The escorts who had been startled by the voice that appeared without warning split apart to either side. Ju Hwaran, however, remained composed.

[P9]
“Yes. They’ve left.”

[P10]
“Are you disappointed?”

[P11]
“I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t.”

[P12]
“It can’t be helped. The people who are going to leave leave, and the people who are going to stay stay. That’s the way of things.”

[P13]
“The way of things…”

[P14]
Ju Hwaran murmured the words quietly, then slowly turned around.

[P15]
“Which side is Captain Song on?”

[P16]
“Me?”

[P17]
Song Ilseom gave a quiet laugh and ostentatiously swung the travel pack over his shoulder.

[P18]
“Which side do you think?”

[P19]
“Is that why you pretended to have passed out drunk?”

[P20]
“It’s been ten years. I’d say I’ve done my duty by now…but is that still not enough?”

[P21]
“No.”

[P22]
“…”

[P23]
“It isn’t enough. You still haven’t done your duty.”

[P24]
Song Ilseom’s brow furrowed at Ju Hwaran’s unhesitating answer.

[P25]
“Still not enough? Even after I protected the Yongbong Escort Bureau—and you—for ten years?”

[P26]
“Can that compare to the debt of gratitude owed for my grandfather’s lifesaving deed?”

[P27]
“You…”

[P28]
Song Ilseom raised his voice and took a step forward. The escorts nearby flinched and gripped their sword hilts.

[P29]
They had not heard the hidden truth of his origins. To them, Song Ilseom was still someone they had to be wary of. In particular, the other two escort captains who belonged to the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts alongside him openly showed their hostility.

[P30]
“Lower your voice. It won’t do you any good.”

[P31]
“We don’t know what the Young Bureau Head thinks, but we’re not convinced. No matter how we look at it, there’s something suspicious about you.”

[P32]
The two escort captains stood in Song Ilseom’s way with grim expressions.

[P33]
“Enough. Step aside.”

[P34]
At Ju Hwaran’s calm voice, the two escort captains stammered.

[P35]
“Y-Young Bureau Head.”

[P36]
“But this man hasn’t completely cleared himself of suspicion yet—!”

[P37]
“I said step aside. I have something important to discuss with him, so everyone return to your posts and take care of the remaining work.”

[P38]
“Hmm…”

[P39]
“Y-yes, ma’am.”

[P40]
The two escort captains moved their lips as if they still had something to say, then slowly nodded.

[P41]
Song Ilseom watched their backs as they walked away with the other escorts. Then he clicked his tongue at Ju Hwaran.

[P42]
“I can’t tell whether they’re loyal or stupid. They’ve come this far and still can’t tell friend from foe.”

[P43]
“Your premise is wrong.”

[P44]
“What?”

[P45]
“They aren’t loyal or stupid, as you assume, Captain Song.”

[P46]
A question flashed through Song Ilseom’s mind.

[P47]
*Could it be?*

[P48]
The insight came in an instant.

[P49]
He was a born fighter and a martial artist through and through, but that did not mean he was stupid.

[P50]
Once he understood the situation, Song Ilseom muttered quietly,

[P51]
“Well, this is a real mess.”

[P52]
Ju Hwaran nodded.

[P53]
“They deliberately ruined escort missions and contracts, siphoned off funds in the confusion, and manipulated the ledgers with great care. There’s no way Uncle Heo did all of this alone.”

[P54]
“Just how far does this conspiracy reach?”

[P55]
“We’ll have to determine the exact number and identities from this point forward…but at the very least, we should include two people.”

[P56]
Ju Hwaran’s gaze swept over the backs of the two escort captains as they grew more distant, then settled on Song Ilseom.

[P57]
“I’m going to root them out completely.”

[P58]
“Why didn’t you reveal it right there after the Chief Escort was killed?”

[P59]
“The confusion would only have grown worse. Besides, if I can’t accomplish even this with my own strength, I have no right to become the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”

[P60]
“Are you confident?”

[P61]
Ju Hwaran stared at Song Ilseom in silence.

[P62]
“How about putting away that travel pack you’re carrying and taking it out again a year from now?”

[P63]
“You want to use me to root them out?”

[P64]
“Captain Song, I need a blade sharp enough to cut down anyone right now. As it happens, the right person is standing right in front of me.”

[P65]
“I refuse. And stop calling me Captain.”

[P66]
“Then how about hiring the Soul-Chasing Guest?”

[P67]
“What?”

[P68]
Ju Hwaran shrugged.

[P69]
“The Soul-Chasing Guest of the world won’t be cheap…but given your connection to our family, perhaps you’ll make an exception?”

[P70]
“So I’m supposed to repay the life-saving kindness that way?”

[P71]
“If that were the case, I would have asked for something much bigger.”

[P72]
“A moment ago, you said I still hadn’t done my duty in return for the Escort King’s lifesaving grace.”

[P73]
“That was because there were too many eyes watching us. My grandfather told me as well. He said that all he had done was save another person.”

[P74]
“Ha!”

[P75]
Song Ilseom burst out laughing.

[P76]
Ten years ago, Junzi Sword Ju Hogun had said the same thing to the young man who had come to him carrying a faded jade hairpin.

[P77]
“Though we met a generation apart, you came to find us in the end. That’s enough. Don’t let the ties of the previous generation bind you. Live your own life.”

[P78]
“Pardon?”

[P79]
“My father told me that what he had done was simply save another person. I feel the same way. And…thank you for growing into such a fine young man.”

[P80]
It had been a shock.

[P81]
From childhood onward, Song Ilseom’s life had been one continuous struggle. His parents had died young, and when his only support—his grandmother—passed away as well, he had to make his way alone without anyone to help him.

[P82]
He had stolen weapons from piles of corpses, cut down wandering martial artists who tried to rob him of his rightful pay, and proven himself through countless life-and-death duels.

[P83]
*I thought he would ask me for something.*

[P84]
To Song Ilseom, who had lived as a wandering martial artist, that was only natural.

[P85]
If Ju Hogun had wanted him to eliminate someone, Song Ilseom would have done it willingly. It would have left a bad taste in his mouth, but it was something he had always done.

[P86]
One more among the countless requests he had completed.

[P87]
But Ju Hogun had been different.

[P88]
He was the first “adult” Song Ilseom had met after becoming an orphan with no one in the world.

[P89]
Maybe that was why the words had slipped out before he could think.

[P90]
“Ten years.”

[P91]
“Hmm?”

[P92]
“I’ll leave after ten years. Though all I know is how to kill people, I’ll protect you and your child no matter what happens. Just as the Escort King did several decades ago.”

[P93]
Song Ilseom kept his oath.

[P94]
He became an escort of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and faithfully followed orders. While he remained at the bureau, he followed the Chief’s daughter like a shadow and protected her at his request.

[P95]
As the years passed and the child grew into a beautiful young lady, strange rumors circulated about the two of them, but he paid them no mind.

[P96]
Whether the Chief collapsed or the Escort Bureau fell apart, Song Ilseom silently remained in place.

[P97]
*I’m only doing my duty.*

[P98]
Song Ilseom opened his tightly shut eyes. Then he abruptly spoke to Ju Hwaran, who had been watching him.

[P99]
“I’m leaving in a month.”

[P100]
“…”

[P101]
“If you discover the identities of the traitors, I’ll lead the way and weed them out. A month will be enough.”

[P102]
Seeing Ju Hwaran’s expression, Song Ilseom spoke bluntly.

[P103]
“Don’t make that face. I’m only going to Xianyang to pick up an elixir and bring it back.”

[P104]
“An elixir?”

[P105]
“That’s right. It should be able to cure the Chief’s illness. The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was too potent and might have the opposite effect, but the elixir I obtained this time should definitely work.”

[P106]
“H-how did you get an elixir like that…?”

[P107]
“Enough. I’m tired of talking, so don’t ask any more questions.”

[P108]
Song Ilseom waved a hand.

[P109]
It was an elixir he had managed to acquire after searching for more than two years. It was not a legendary elixir like the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, but it was better suited than anything else to restoring the Chief, who had fallen into qi deviation.

[P110]
He had been forced to pour every last bit of the enormous fortune he had earned as the Soul-Chasing Guest into it, but money could always be earned again.

[P111]
“Do you know something?”

[P112]
Song Ilseom’s calm voice continued.

[P113]
“There’s nothing more difficult than saving a person’s life. What came naturally to you…was the hardest thing for me.”

[P114]
Song Ilseom had made a living by killing people.

[P115]
It was only after joining the Yongbong Escort Bureau that he began protecting someone instead.

[P116]
“Captain Song…”

[P117]
Ju Hwaran stared at him with moist eyes, but when she saw his furrowed brow, she hastily corrected herself.

[P118]
“Ah, Great Hero Song.”

[P119]
“How long are you going to keep getting confused?”

[P120]
“I’m sorry. I was so surprised that I said it without thinking…”

[P121]
“Then why don’t you create a position while you’re at it?”

[P122]
“Pardon?”

[P123]
“I don’t want to be Chief Escort. I’m terrible at escort missions, and that position requires managing people.”

[P124]
“Yes, yes?”

[P125]
“Guard Hall Master. Yes, that sounds good.”

[P126]
While Ju Hwaran was still stammering, Song Ilseom turned around and began walking away.

[P127]
Not toward the gate outside, where darkness had settled, but toward his own quarters.

[P128]
“I shouldn’t have packed the travel bag.”

[P129]
As she watched Song Ilseom’s back recede with those quiet words trailing behind him, dimples appeared beside Ju Hwaran’s mouth.

[P130]
* * *

[P131]
Whoosh!

[P132]
With taut rigging and sterns slicing through the current, the fast ships surged forward like the wind. Men with their bronze-colored upper bodies bare pulled ropes and rowed oars. At least fifty men were visible on the deck of each ship.

[P133]
There were five fast ships in all, meaning they had nearly three hundred men.

[P134]
“Faster! Faster!”

[P135]
“You louts! How can you call yourselves members of the Water Dragon Stronghold when you’re this slow?”

[P136]
The Water Dragon Stronghold was a major river fortress belonging to the Yangtze River Channel League.

[P137]
Its members proudly called themselves the heroes of the Yangtze, but the name used by ordinary people was a great deal less flattering.

[P138]
“River bandits! They’re river bandits!”

[P139]
“Why the hell are those bastards here?”

[P140]
The shipmaster who spotted the five fast ships promptly collapsed into his seat.

[P141]
His opponents were not some band of random thugs, but the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There was no way to outrun their fast ships, and he could not even dream of fighting them.

[P142]
*This day has gone completely to hell.*

[P143]
No. There was only one way to get through this quietly, at least.

[P144]
The shipmaster called over the youngest sailor passing by with a dejected look on his face.

[P145]
“Hey!”

[P146]
“Yes, shipmaster.”

[P147]
“Tell the passengers to pay up.”

[P148]
“Pardon?”

[P149]
“Collect the money! They have to pay the toll, don’t they?”

[P150]
The fact that they belonged to the Yangtze River Channel League was both unfortunate and fortunate. Once they were caught, there was no way to escape, but they did not simply swing their swords without reason.

[P151]
The Yangtze River Channel League insisted that they were in a different class from the common river-bandit rabble found everywhere under heaven, but in the end, one was no different from the other.

[P152]
“Phew… I’ve really lost today’s business.”

[P153]
The shipmaster was sighing deeply when someone tapped him on the shoulder.

[P154]
“Excuse me.”

[P155]
“Gah! You startled me! Who are you?”

[P156]
“I’m a passenger.”

[P157]
“I know that.”

[P158]
The shipmaster looked at the young man who had appeared out of nowhere. Judging by the sword at his waist, he seemed to be a martial artist, but…

[P159]
*He looks kind of dumb. With that protruding mouth, he looks like he talks a lot, too.*

[P160]
Third Rate martial artists were a dime a dozen.

[P161]
It wasn’t as if he had never dealt with one or two of them before. The shipmaster sighed and opened his mouth.

[P162]
“Why did you come over? If this is about collecting money, I have nothing to say, so go back to your seat. Don’t try anything stupid and end up crossing the Sanzu River.”[^1]

[P163]
The young man watched the fast ships drawing rapidly closer.

[P164]
“Are they river bandits?”

[P165]
“Can’t you tell by looking? They’re the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There isn’t a person in Sichuan who doesn’t know them.”

[P166]
“The Yangtze River Channel League…”

[P167]
“Running won’t help. You’ll never escape those fast ships. Once they spot you, it’s over. Completely over!”

[P168]
“That ship must be pretty fast.”

[P169]
“What kind of question is—”

[P170]
The shipmaster was about to answer irritably when he suddenly sucked in a breath and closed his mouth.

[P171]
A shadow rose behind the young man, a full head taller than him.

[P172]
The man had shaggy hair, and a great mound of hides rose high above the pack frame on his back.

[P173]
The giant stared blankly at the shipmaster, then spoke to the young man.

[P174]
“Mujin.”

[P175]
“Yes?”

[P176]
“Let’s take that ship.”

[P177]
The shipmaster wondered if he had heard correctly.

[P178]
[^1]: The Sanzu River is a Buddhist river believed to mark the boundary between life and death.

[P140]
*This day has gone completely to hell.*

[P141]
There was only one way to get through this quietly.

[P142]

[P143]
“Hey!”

[P144]
“Yes, shipmaster.”

[P145]
“Tell the passengers to pay up.”

[P146]
“Pardon?”

[P147]

[P148]

[P149]

[P150]
“Damn it… There goes today’s profit.”

[P151]
The shipmaster was heaving sigh after sigh when someone tapped him on the shoulder.

[P152]
“Excuse me.”

[P153]
“Gah! You startled me! Who are you?”

[P154]
“I’m a passenger.”

[P155]
“I know that.”

[P156]

[P157]

[P158]

[P159]

[P160]

[P161]

[P162]

[P163]

[P165]

[P166]

[P167]

[P168]

[P169]

[P170]

[P171]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
